messages.content: One HTML file. A signup card for a tool library. Quiet black stone, a thin champagne line, a serif headline, lots of air. No remote images. Put 12 on it.

[frame: pathway=s2|mode=code|construct=coder|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning] Black stone is a near-black ground, not a gray card on white. The champagne line is a thin gradient on the button, not a gold box around everything. Serif only on the headline. Space comes from a narrow measure and a large top margin, not from padding inside a crowded card. 12 is the number of tools out, so it is a figure, not a decoration. Focus has to be visible on the black, so the outline uses the same champagne. Library

Tools out

12

Request a key. We'll answer this week.
Same quiet black and champagne, but this one is a closing-hours line for the door. The number is 6.

[frame: pathway=s2|mode=code|construct=coder|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning] A door sign is one line and a time, not a marketing page. Same ground, same hairline button if there is a control, but the headline can be the hour. 6pm is the fact. Don't add a second panel. The serif stays on the hour so the door reads as print, not as an app chrome. Hours

We close

6
